persona.bio: Owns a small women's clothing boutique, just her and two part timers. Working the floor, buying at markets twice a year, posting new arrivals on Instagram, steaming and tagging stock, window displays every month, payroll and paying vendors, answering DMs about sizes and holds. She does most of it on her iPhone between customers. Instagram and the DMs take the most time, then tagging stock. She uses ChatGPT some weeks for captions and Canva's AI for posts.

steps.note: I own a small women’s clothing boutique with two part time helpers. I write to customers who message me on Instagram and by text, and to regulars I know well. I like a warm, friendly tone that sounds like me, with short messages that get to the point. For captions, I like a light, simple voice that describes the piece without big claims. Never add details I did not give you, like sizes, prices, fabrics or hours. If something is missing, ask me or leave a bracket I can fill in. Keep it plain, with no hype and no long paragraphs. Give me one version unless I ask for more.

steps.title: Your customer messages, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your replies live on your phone’s keyboard, each one a few letters away. When a customer asks about a size or a hold, you type a short shortcut and tap the reply instead of writing it again. It works in Instagram DMs and texts alike, and you still change the details before you send.

safeUse: Never type a customer’s full name, phone number, address or payment details into a chat tool. Use brackets instead.
Don’t paste in anything from Square, like card details or customer purchase records.
Keep supplier names, order numbers and wholesale prices out of your chats unless you are comfortable sharing them.
Read every caption and reply before you post or send it, and check sizes, prices and hours yourself.
Only use details you know are true about your pieces, like fabric or fit, and fix anything the AI guessed.

design.today: You answer customer messages many times a day, each one from scratch. They reach you by Instagram DMs, text messages and walk in asks, and you work from your phone only.
design.newWay: Your most common replies, like size checks, holds and opening hours, are saved on your phone and are a few letters away. You tap one in, change the item or size, and send it yourself. Messages that are not routine you still answer in your own words, so the quick ones stop eating your day.

steps.goal: Pick the ten questions customers ask you most, like size checks, holds, restocks and opening hours.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you can draft replies there.
Save a short note about your boutique and how you like to sound, so every draft reads like you.
Paste in your real past replies and ask for a clean, short version of each of the ten answers with gaps for item and size.
Save the ten replies so each one is a few letters away in Instagram DMs and text messages.

material.label: Ten saved replies
material.what: Short answers to your most common questions, with gaps for the item, size and hold time.

material.label: Tone notes
material.what: A few lines on how you talk to customers, so drafts sound warm and like you.

material.label: Shortcut list
material.what: A list of the letters that bring up each saved reply.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply and fill in the item, size and hold time before you send it.

design.today: You text your regulars often, each message written fresh.
design.newWay: You keep a saved assistant in ChatGPT that knows your boutique and your voice. You tell it what you want to say, like new arrivals or a restock, and it gives you a friendly text you can adjust for each regular. You stay in charge of who gets which message and when, and the texts keep sounding personal.

steps.goal: Make a project for regular customer texts so your instructions and examples stay in one place.
Choose three or four past texts to regulars that sounded most like you.
Set up the assistant with those examples so it drafts new regular texts in your voice from a few words of input.
Try it with a real upcoming message, like a new arrival, and adjust the instructions until the draft feels right.

material.label: Assistant instructions
material.what: What your boutique sells, who your regulars are in general terms, and how long and friendly the texts should be.

material.label: Example texts
material.what: Your three or four best past texts to regulars, with no customer private details.

material.label: Quick prompt
material.what: A short line to fill in each time, like the item, the occasion and any offer.

design.checkPoint: You read each draft, check the item, price and any names, and send it yourself from your phone.
